history.summary: A 2023-completed 1BR in the very large Normanton Park (D05, near One-North/Kent Ridge) at a low $850k / $1613 psf — but the resale-only rate is NEGATIVE (-1.3%) over a massive, highly-reliable 1225 transactions, signalling post-completion price softness as the huge unit supply gets absorbed. Deep liquidity, but the data says owners are currently selling flat-to-down.
history.rating_rationale: The 1225-txn series is the most reliable in this batch, and it shows resale-only at -1.3% — the mega-development's own supply is weighing on prices post-TOP. $1613 psf is well below the $1994 median (the discount reflects this softness, not a steal). Pros: very liquid (huge dev), low $850k quantum, real D05/One-North/CRL location. But buying into a project actively printing flat-to-negative resale is a Neutral, not a Buy — wait for the supply overhang to clear.

history.summary: Cheap, verified 1BR in a young D05 (OCR) mega-project near one-north/Kent Ridge — asking $1,613 psf sits at the very bottom of the project's $1,613-$2,446 PSF range, with the deepest dataset in this batch (1,225 resale txns). OCR location plus a real entry-PSF discount carry the case.
history.rating_rationale: The asking $1,613 psf is exactly at the floor of the current project PSF range ($1,613-$2,446) and well under the 6-12 month average of ~$2,064-$2,093 psf, so age_adj_premium of -20.5% and psf_premium_vs_cohort of -13.7% are credible. Crucially the appreciation_source is ura_resale_only over 1,225 txns — the deepest, cleanest signal here — so even the slightly negative -1.27% reads as honest resale-to-resale data rather than a launch-inflated CAGR. D05 is OCR/RCR-fringe (best realized forward returns under v3.4), the $850k quantum is liquid, and there are no red flags. The negative trailing number is de-weighted; the value entry and location drive the Buy.
red_flags: Slightly negative trailing resale appreciation (-1.27%) shows the project has not been a price outperformer recently
~1,862-unit mega-development — heavy concurrent 1BR resale/rental supply on exit
527 sqft compact 1BR; tenant pool limited to singles/couples

Entry at the floor of the project PSF range gives a verified margin of safety

history.summary: The 2026-06-09 Buy was a since-removed $0.85M 1BR at $1,613psf; the current unit is one of only 22 strata terrace townhouses (3-storey, 2,110 sqft) asking $3.8M / $1,801psf — ABOVE the cohort all-time-high print of $1,721psf (Aug 2025, the only same-size transaction in 12 months). Its apparent cheapness vs the ~$2,100+ apartment-pooled median is the v3.6 strata-format artifact, not value.
history.rating_rationale: Validated cheap-vs-SAME-SIZE-peers signal is negative: ask is ~4.6% above the record terrace print and the cohort transacts ~once a year, so the mega-project 1,225-txn liquidity does not apply to this format. $3.8M quantum + niche 3-storey townhouse + no walkable MRT thins both exit and tenant pools; gross yield ~2.7-2.8% at plausible $8-9k rent. D05/OCR +3.7%/yr forward tailwind is real but is the region effect already in the price — it does not justify paying above the cohort high. Algo 478 (below market-typical) is directionally right here.
red_flags: Asking $1,801psf exceeds the all-time-high same-size print ($1,721psf, Aug 2025) — premium, not discount
Strata terrace format: 22-unit cohort, ~1 transaction/yr — illiquid despite mega-project headline depth
$3.8M quantum + no MRT in walking distance thins buyer/tenant pool; ~2.7% gross yield
Project trailing resale appreciation negative (-1.3% over 1,225 txns)
Apparent cheapness vs pooled median is a strata-vs-apartment benchmarking artifact (v3.6)
catalysts: D05/OCR among strongest realized forward-return regions (+3.7%/yr)
one-north/NUS/Kent Ridge tenant catchment supports family-rental demand
Rare landed-like format inside a condo could attract a niche own-stay buyer at the right price (~$3.5M or below)
